tags: why does my dog get hyper at night
script: Every evening, right around the same time, your calm, quiet dog suddenly turns into a completely different animal, sprinting around the house, grabbing toys, and demanding attention out of nowhere. This is sometimes nicknamed the witching hour, and it's an incredibly common pattern. Part of it is simply built-up energy, many dogs spend the day fairly calm at home while their owners are busy, and evening is when the household finally slows down and becomes available, which naturally triggers a release of pent-up energy. There's also a genuine biological piece, dogs have crepuscular tendencies inherited from their wild ancestors, meaning they're naturally more alert and active around dawn and dusk. Evening also often lines up with dinner time and a bigger drop in outdoor temperature, both of which can add an extra layer of energy and excitement. If this burst is disruptive, the most effective fix usually isn't punishment, it's proactively working in a walk, play session, or training exercise earlier in the day so that pent-up energy has somewhere healthier to go before it reaches full evening chaos mode.
